findings.claim: L77 is a single very long paragraph packing two owner quotes, the full terse-style proposal, the rule text, an approval and a status decision. The approved lint rule and the still-pending style text are mixed, so a reader cannot quickly tell which parts are approved (rule for T26, Codex persona removal in T22) and which wait (style text, T27 (a), Codex persona part of T31). Splitting into approved and pending items, as L76 does with numbered points, would help.

The entry says 'The gentle persona text in ~/.codex/agents.md leaves in T22 (yes to L76 risk 1, replaced by the labdrian style)' while also saying the Codex persona part of T31/T22 waits on the style approval. Whether the removal in T22 is blocked or proceeds is ambiguous, and the replacement style is not yet approved. The Specs/Tasks for T22/T27/T31 are not updated in this commit, so the log entry and tasks may diverge. It also states 'si me fyst' is read as 'si me gusta', an interpretation that is recorded but flagged only parenthetically.

evidence: The diff only appends one log entry (L77) to odd/tasks/labdrian-orchestrator-opencode.md; no code is changed.
The commit message claims it records the terse style request and the lint rule, and the entry does so.
L77 reopens the L64 approval and references L60, L64, L76, T22, T26, T27 and T31; these were not verifiable from the diff alone.
